--- title: "Extra_1: Time on the Horizon: ggHoriPlot methods" author: "Yiqiong PAN" date: "27 Feb, 2026" date-modified: last-modified execute: echo: true # display the code eval: true # run the code message: false warning: false freeze: true # do not re-render if nothing edited format: html: toc: true code-link: true number-sections: true number-depth: 6 editor: visual --- ## Learning Outcome A horizon graph is a multi-panel area chart that visualises a numeric data over a continuous interval such as a time period. It is useful for understanding the overall trend, patterns and outliers in the data. ## Getting Started ### Installing and Loading the Required Libraries There are **4** packages that will be used in this exercise. | Package | Description | |------------------------------------|------------------------------------| | [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) | A collection of R packages for data importing, cleaning, transformation, and visualisation (e.g., [readr](https://readr.tidyverse.org/), dplyr, tidyr, [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/)). | | [lubridate](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lubridate/index.html) | A Tidyverse package that handles date-time objects | | [ggthemes](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggthemes/index.html) | Provides 'ggplot2' themes and scales that replicate some of the famous looks. | | [ggHoriPlot](https://rivasiker.github.io/ggHoriPlot/) | Extends horizon plots in ggplot2 | The code below installs and loads the required packages into R environment. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggthemes,lubridate, ggHoriPlot) ``` ::: ## Step 1: Data Import For this hands-on exercise, the [**Average Retail Prices of Selected Consumer Items**](https://tablebuilder.singstat.gov.sg/page-not-found) file will be used. It contains 7,452 rows of time series records of average retail prices for selected consumer items. ### Importing the Data We use `read_csv()` from the **readr** package to import the dataset *AVERP.csv* into the R environment as a tibble named `df`. We then preview the dataset using `kable()`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} averp <- read_csv("data/AVERP.csv") ``` ::: The dataset contains three columns: two categorical variables, **Date** and **Consumer Items**, and one numeric column **Values**. Since we want to perform time series plotting, it is essential to convert the **Date** to proper date data type. Here we use [`dmy()`](https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/reference/ymd.html) from [**lubridate**](https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/) pacakge to convert the column into date format. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} averp <- averp %>% mutate(`Date` = dmy(`Date`)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(averp$`Consumer Items`) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(averp$Date) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Date" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(head(averp), "html") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Date Consumer Items Values
2014-01-01 Wholemeal Bread (Per 400 Gram) 2.05
2014-02-01 Wholemeal Bread (Per 400 Gram) 2.05
2014-03-01 Wholemeal Bread (Per 400 Gram) 2.04
2014-04-01 Wholemeal Bread (Per 400 Gram) 2.04
2014-05-01 Wholemeal Bread (Per 400 Gram) 2.05
2014-06-01 Wholemeal Bread (Per 400 Gram) 2.05
````` ::: ::: ### Step 2. Plotting the horizon graph **Horizon plots** compare each consumer item to its own history/pattern of average retail prices while **line plots** with same scales compare the average prices to each other. The code below creates a horizon plot by using [`geom_horizon()`](https://rivasiker.github.io/ggHoriPlot/reference/geom_horizon.html) from [**ggHoriPlot**](https://rivasiker.github.io/ggHoriPlot/index.html) package. "%b%y" in `date_labels` controls the format of date that displays under the x-axis. "3-month" of `date_breaks`set the labels only shows every 3 months. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} averp %>% filter(Date >= "2018-01-01") %>% ggplot() + geom_horizon(aes(x = Date, y = Values), origin = "midpoint", horizonscale = 6) + facet_grid(`Consumer Items`~.) + theme_few() + scale_fill_hcl(palette = 'RdBu') + theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(0, "lines"), strip.text.y = element_text( size = 5, angle = 0, hjust = 0 ), legend.position = 'none', axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7), axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) + scale_x_date(expand = c(0,0), date_breaks = "3 month", date_labels = "%b%y") + ggtitle('Average Retail Prices of Selected Consumer Items(Jan 2018 to Dec 2022)') ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Extra_1_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Reference Kam, Tin Seong (2026). 18 Time on the Horizon: ggHoriPlot methods, R for Visual Analytics, https://r4va.netlify.app/chap18
